glossary.definition: Action to eliminate a detected nonconformity (ISO 9000 as quoted in the ISO/IAF APG paper).
Action to eliminate the cause of a nonconformity and prevent recurrence.
Immediate steps that limit the effect of a finding while its cause is investigated.
Follow-up evidence check that a corrective action prevented recurrence before closure.
The role responsible for decisions and records in the defined workflow.
Non-fulfillment of a requirement (ISO 9000 as cited in the APG paper).
Requirements without which the CAPA workflow fails, such as linking findings to specific requirements or separating implementation and verification roles.
A vendor evaluation session structured around the buyer's workflow decision sequence and anonymized representative data rather than vendor marketing scripts.
A workflow permission rule preventing the person who implements a corrective action from approving or verifying its effectiveness.
The ability to reconstruct the complete chronological history of a finding, including containment, cause, actions, approvals, and effectiveness evidence.
Whether the root cause was eliminated and recurrence prevented by the actions taken, verified through objective evidence.
Pre-established, measurable specifications detailing the measure, scope, and duration needed to confirm that a nonconformity's cause has been eliminated.
Objective records, observations, or measurement data gathered after action implementation to verify that effectiveness criteria were met.
A compiled record summarizing the finding, cause analysis, completed actions, and verification results reviewed prior to authorizing final closure.
Historical quality records, logs, emails, or paper reports created prior to implementing the new CAPA software.
A standardized dropdown list or taxonomy (such as source, significance, or cause categories) used to normalize legacy data during migration.
A scoped test execution of legacy data migration into a non-production test environment to validate mapping rules and error handling before cutover.
A designated timeframe prior to cutover during which no new data entries are permitted in legacy sources to ensure migration completeness.
The formal transition point where legacy recordkeeping is discontinued and active CAPA workflows commence in the new software.

example.label: Illustrative example
example.description: An unnamed Canadian manufacturer evaluates CAPA software for one recurring inspection finding, following it through containment, cause investigation, action, effectiveness review and closure; all situations and records are hypothetical, not customer results.

reviewedChapters.title: Mapping the current workflow: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The guide page adheres strictly to its assigned scope, chapter plan, and boundaries. All cited primary sources (ISO/IAF APG Documenting Nonconformity and NIST RPD-G-07) are accurately quoted with proper disclaimers, external links match research sources, and internal references maintain appropriate caution regarding software capabilities. The text systematically develops workflow mapping from problem definition through handoff mapping, decision ownership, and acceptance criteria using a consistent, clearly labeled hypothetical machining manufacturer scenario.
decisions: Is this a real nonconformity?
How significant is it?
What must be isolated now? / What is contained, and by whom?
What question will the investigation answer? / Who investigates?
Who does what by when? / Who approves the action plan?
Was the action carried out as described?
Is the finding closed, or reopened? / Who confirms closure?

reviewedChapters.title: Evaluating software capabilities: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The chapter adheres rigorously to its assigned scope and outline, providing practical, actionable guidance for evaluating CAPA software without making unsubstantiated product claims. Citations to ISO/IAF APG Nonconformity Documenting and NIST RPD-G-08 correctly reflect the source materials with appropriate caveats regarding laboratory context and auditor guidance. All four subsections feature clearly labeled illustrative examples centering on the consistent unnamed Canadian machining manufacturer scenario. No unassigned FAQ section is present.
decisions: Confirm or reject a finding as a true nonconformity
Rate significance and route
Record containment as a distinct pre-investigation action
Approve or return action plan
Verify implementation and confirm effectiveness before closing
Reopen closed finding upon recurrence
Score candidate products against must-have criteria

reviewedChapters.title: Recording findings and containment: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The page adheres strictly to its assigned brief, chapter boundaries, and research sources. Factual claims from NIST RPD-G-07, APG Documenting Nonconformity, and APG Review and Closing are accurately quoted and framed with appropriate caveats regarding ISO 9001:2015 auditor guidance and laboratory context. The text covers classification, immediate containment assignment, linking affected records, and checking containment evidence. Practical evaluation criteria, workflow decisions, inputs, roles, records, exceptions, and consistently labeled hypothetical examples featuring an unnamed machining manufacturer are present in each subsection. No unassigned FAQ section was included.
decisions: Confirm or reject whether a deviation is a true nonconformity
Assign significance rating and determine routing path
Define containment scope and boundary
Select containment action and assign authority to execute
Determine required internal and customer notifications
Decide whether to connect records via live integrations or validated manual references
Authorize release of held product or resumption of work
Document override when proceeding past missing containment evidence

reviewedChapters.title: Investigating root causes: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The guide page strictly complies with its assigned scope, chapter plan, and research sources. It provides practical evaluation criteria and workflow guidance for investigating root causes in CAPA software, covering question definition, evidence gathering, competing cause analysis, and cause statement recording. All primary source citations to the ISO/IAF Auditing Practices Group papers are accurate and properly contextualized as auditor guidance. Each subsection features structured workflow evaluation points, clear roles, record inputs/outputs, and consistently labeled illustrative examples using the unnamed machining manufacturer scenario without claiming unverified vendor features. No unassigned FAQ section is included.
decisions: Record chosen investigation depth and justify full investigation versus simple correction
Modify or refine the investigation question midway through an investigation
Log data collection gaps as independent findings requiring follow-up action
Categorize candidate failure factors as not able to confirm, possible, or confirmed
Determine whether a failure mechanism is systemic or accidental
Accept, challenge, or return the root cause statement for additional evidence
Flag related processes, machines, or sites for parallel evaluation

reviewedChapters.title: Planning and implementing corrective actions: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The guide page adheres strictly to its outline, scope boundaries, and research sources. Factual citations to the ISO/IAF Auditing Practices Group guidance on reviewing and closing nonconformities and the NIST RPD-G-08 corrective action procedure are accurately represented with required contextual disclaimers. The four subsections cover connecting actions to causes, assigning owners and deadlines, handling delays, and recording implementation evidence without overstepping into effectiveness review or prior stages. Hypothetical examples featuring the unnamed machining manufacturer scenario are consistently labeled across all subsections, and no unassigned FAQ section is present.
decisions: Deciding whether correction, corrective action, or both are required and recording why
Rejecting improvement proposals from the action plan when they do not link to the accepted cause
Accepting or refusing an assigned action ownership and due date
Approving or returning an action plan prior to implementation
Approving or rejecting an action due date extension request
Establishing interim containment protection during an action delay
Prioritizing actions and findings during resource conflicts
Approving or rejecting action cancellation requests
Confirming implementation evidence matches the plan prior to marking an action complete
Returning an action as incomplete due to missing implementation evidence

reviewedChapters.title: Reviewing corrective action effectiveness: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The guide page strictly complies with its assigned scope, chapter plan, and primary source materials. It addresses defining effectiveness criteria, choosing follow-up evidence, reopening ineffective actions, and authorizing closure within CAPA software evaluation workflows. Citations to ISO/IAF Auditing Practices Group guidance on nonconformity review and closing and the NIST RPD-G-08 corrective action procedure are accurately represented with proper context. The unnamed machining manufacturer illustrative scenario is consistently maintained across all subsections, and no unassigned FAQ section is present.
decisions: Defining measurable effectiveness criteria and monitoring duration in advance of result review
Selecting follow-up evidence methods proportionate to the finding and aligned to the accepted cause
Deciding whether to extend monitoring or record stated caveats for limited sample sizes
Evaluating whether corrective actions caused unintended side effects or new management system issues
Marking an effectiveness check as failed and reopening the original finding record
Determining whether to re-establish containment after an action fails
Returning to root cause analysis versus replanning actions upon action failure
Escalating recurring failures to wider process reviews after exceeding defined cycle limits
Confirming all closure preconditions are satisfied before authorizing final sign-off
Enforcing separation of duties between the action implementer and the closing authority

reviewedChapters.title: Planning migration and configuration: CAPA software workflows
reviewedChapters.summary: The guide page adheres strictly to the assigned chapter plan, scope boundaries, and primary source materials. Factual citations to the ISO/IAF Auditing Practices Group guidance papers (on documenting nonconformities and reviewing/closing nonconformities) and the NIST RPD-G-08 corrective action procedure are accurately contextualized. Each subsection methodically addresses legacy record inventory, data cleaning, relationship mapping, pilot import verification, cutover scheduling, and rollback recovery planning. All illustrative examples are clearly labeled and consistently follow the unnamed machining manufacturer scenario without asserting unverified software capabilities. No unassigned FAQ section is included.
decisions: Classify legacy records by status and business value to determine migration versus archival scope
Define retention rules and approve legacy records to leave behind or purge
Decide whether unmapped legacy fields should be left blank, filled with marked placeholders, or manually populated
Determine whether legacy record relationships should be rebuilt as relational database links or preserved as plain text
Approve pilot import results and verify discrepancy thresholds before authorizing full cutover
Select cutover strategy (single direct cutover versus phased transition) and schedule freeze window
Define recovery threshold triggers and authorize aborting cutover to roll back to legacy systems
